q: Children Education Allowance in respect of a child with disability is admissible up to the age of:
e: Children Education Allowance for a child with disability continues up to the age of 22 years, beyond the normal age limit applicable to other children.

q: The number of sets of Privilege Ticket Orders (PTOs) admissible to a railway servant in a calendar year is:
e: A railway servant is entitled to four sets of Privilege Ticket Orders (PTOs) in a calendar year for journeys at concessional fares.

q: The statement which is attached to the monthly pay bill of an establishment, showing the particulars of the staff who remained absent, or were on leave, during the month, is known as the:
e: The Absentee Statement attached to the monthly pay bill shows the particulars of staff who were absent or on leave during the month, so that pay is drawn correctly.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund may enhance the amount of his monthly subscription during the course of a financial year:
e: A GPF subscriber may raise his monthly subscription during a financial year, but such enhancement is permitted not more than twice in the year.

q: The monthly subscription payable by a Group 'A' officer under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme is:
e: The monthly subscription under CGEGIS is graded by group, and a Group A officer subscribes at the highest slab of Rs 120 per month.

q: The Productivity Linked Bonus paid to eligible non-gazetted railway employees is:

options.A: Paid under a special scheme in lieu of statutory bonus, as the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 does not apply to railway employees
options.B: Paid under the provisions of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965
options.C: Paid as part of the wages under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936
options.D: Paid only to the running staff categories

e: Railway employees are outside the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, so Productivity Linked Bonus is paid to them under a special scheme in lieu of statutory bonus.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, where the number of persons employed in an establishment is one thousand or more, the wages for a wage period must be paid before the expiry of the:

options.A: Seventh day after the last day of the wage period
options.B: Tenth day after the last day of the wage period
options.C: Fifteenth day after the last day of the wage period
options.D: Last day of the wage period itself

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, where 1,000 or more persons are employed, wages for a wage period must be paid before the expiry of the tenth day after the last day of the wage period.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after completing full qualifying service. His average emoluments are Rs 72,000 per month. The amount of his monthly pension will be:
e: Pension is 50 per cent of average emoluments for full qualifying service: 50 per cent of Rs 72,000 = Rs 36,000 per month.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 90,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate will be:
e: Family pension at the normal rate is 30 per cent of the last pay drawn: 30 per cent of Rs 90,000 = Rs 27,000 per month.

q: A railway servant retires after rendering 33 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 80,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments for each six-monthly period: 33 years = 66 periods, so 80,000/4 x 66 = Rs 13,20,000, which equals the ceiling of 16.5 times emoluments.

q: A railway pensioner who has commuted a portion of his pension is entitled to Dearness Relief calculated on:

options.A: The reduced pension actually drawn by him after commutation
options.B: The commuted portion of the pension only
options.C: Fifty per cent of the original basic pension
options.D: The original basic pension, including the portion commuted

e: Dearness Relief is calculated on the original basic pension including the commuted portion, so commutation does not reduce the amount on which relief is paid.

q: Under the Railway Pension Rules, the grant of pension to a railway servant is subject to the implied condition of:

options.A: Future good conduct, and the pension may be withheld or withdrawn if the pensioner is convicted of a serious crime or is found guilty of grave misconduct
options.B: The pensioner residing permanently at his home town
options.C: The pensioner not accepting any private employment after retirement
options.D: The pensioner furnishing a life certificate every month

e: Pension is granted subject to the implied condition of future good conduct, and it may be withheld or withdrawn on conviction for a serious crime or grave misconduct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Resignation from railway service ordinarily entails forfeiture of past service and of the pensionary benefits earned by it.
2. Where the resignation is a 'technical resignation' tendered to take up another Government appointment with proper permission, the past service is not forfeited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: resignation normally forfeits past service, but a technical resignation taken with proper permission to join another Government post preserves the past service.

q: Constant Attendant Allowance is admissible to a railway pensioner who:

options.A: Is granted pension on account of 100 per cent disablement and is certified by the competent medical authority to require the services of an attendant
options.C: Retires after rendering 33 years of qualifying service

e: Constant Attendant Allowance is payable to a pensioner with 100 per cent disablement who is certified by the competent medical authority to need the constant services of an attendant.

q: Under the State Railway Provident Fund Rules, the Deposit Linked Insurance amount payable on the death of a subscriber while in service is:

options.A: Equal to the subscription paid by the subscriber in the last year of his service
options.B: Payable in addition to the balance at his credit, and is linked to the average balance in his Fund account during the preceding three years, subject to a prescribed ceiling
options.C: Payable only where the death occurs in the course of duty
options.D: Equal to twelve months' pay of the subscriber in all cases

e: Under SRPF, Deposit Linked Insurance is payable in addition to the balance at credit, linked to the average balance in the account during the preceding three years, subject to a ceiling.

q: A railway servant who retires from service with qualifying service of less than 10 years is paid, in lieu of pension, a service gratuity calculated at the rate of:

options.A: One month's emoluments for each completed year of service
options.B: Half month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service
options.C: Two months' emoluments for each completed year of service
options.D: One-fourth of emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service

e: With less than 10 years of qualifying service there is no pension; instead, service gratuity is paid at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of service.

q: Where both the father and the mother of an eligible child were railway servants and both of them have died, the child is entitled to draw:

options.A: Family pension in respect of the father only
options.B: Family pension in respect of the mother only
options.C: Family pension in respect of either parent, whichever is higher
options.D: Two family pensions, one in respect of each parent, subject to the prescribed overall ceiling

e: An eligible child of two deceased railway servants can draw two family pensions, one in respect of each parent, subject to the prescribed overall ceiling.

q: Government dues outstanding against a retired railway servant, such as arrears of licence fee for the railway accommodation occupied by him, can be recovered from:

options.A: His monthly pension, without any limit
options.B: The Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity payable to him
options.C: The Provident Fund balance of his spouse

e: Outstanding Government dues of a retired servant, such as licence fee arrears for railway accommodation, are recovered from the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity payable to him.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, a subscriber may, at the time of his superannuation, withdraw as a lump sum up to the following proportion of his individual corpus:
e: At superannuation under the Unified Pension Scheme, the subscriber may withdraw as lump sum up to 60 per cent of his individual corpus.

q: Rule 3(1) of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 requires every railway servant at all times to maintain:

options.A: Absolute integrity and devotion to duty
options.B: A bank balance equal to three months' pay
options.C: Membership of a recognised staff association
options.D: Residence within the limits of his station of posting

e: Rule 3(1) of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 requires every railway servant to maintain absolute integrity and devotion to duty at all times.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not communicate, directly or indirectly, any official document or information to:

options.B: The Accounts Officer of his office
options.D: Any person to whom he is not authorised to communicate such document or information

e: The Conduct Rules bar a servant from communicating any official document or information, directly or indirectly, to any person to whom he is not authorised to communicate it.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not, without the previous sanction of the Government:

options.A: Purchase a house site for his own residence
options.B: Engage directly or indirectly in any trade or business, or undertake any other employment
options.C: Open a savings bank account in his own name
options.D: Purchase a motor car for his personal use

e: A railway servant cannot engage in any trade or business, directly or indirectly, or take up other employment, without the previous sanction of the Government.

q: A Group 'A' railway officer who has retired from service shall not accept any commercial employment, without the previous sanction of the Government, before the expiry of the following period from the date of his retirement:
e: A retired Group A officer cannot accept commercial employment within one year of retirement without the previous sanction of the Government.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, in the matter of political activities, a railway servant:

options.A: May join a political party but shall not hold any office in it
options.B: May contest elections to a local body while remaining in service
options.C: Shall not be a member of, or be otherwise associated with, any political party or any organisation which takes part in politics
options.D: May canvass for a candidate outside office hours

e: A railway servant is barred from being a member of, or otherwise associated with, any political party or organisation that takes part in politics.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not:

options.A: Participate in the staff welfare activities of his office
options.B: Resort to, or in any way abet, any form of strike or coercion in connection with any matter pertaining to his service or to the service of any other railway servant
options.C: Represent his grievances through his recognised staff association
options.D: Attend the meetings of his staff association

e: The Conduct Rules prohibit a railway servant from resorting to, or in any way abetting, any form of strike or coercion in connection with service matters.

q: A railway servant who has been placed under suspension shall not, during the period of suspension:

options.A: Leave his headquarters without obtaining the previous permission of the authority which placed him under suspension
options.C: Submit a representation against the order of suspension
options.D: Take the assistance of a defence assistant in the inquiry against him

e: During suspension the servant remains under discipline and cannot leave his headquarters without the previous permission of the authority which placed him under suspension.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A major penalty can be imposed on a railway servant without holding an inquiry where he is dismissed or removed on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge.
2. An inquiry can also be dispensed with where the disciplinary authority is satisfied, for reasons to be recorded by it in writing, that it is not reasonably practicable to hold such an inquiry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: inquiry is dispensed with where penalty follows conviction on a criminal charge, and also where the disciplinary authority records in writing that holding an inquiry is not reasonably practicable.

q: In manpower planning on the Railways, the norms laid down for assessing the requirement of staff for a particular activity with reference to the workload are known as:
e: In manpower planning, the approved norms for assessing staff requirement of an activity by reference to its workload are called yardsticks.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant retains his lien on a post while he is on deputation or on foreign service.
2. The lien of a railway servant on a post stands terminated as soon as he is appointed substantively to another permanent post.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: the servant retains his lien on his post while on deputation or foreign service, and the lien terminates once he is appointed substantively to another permanent post.

q: Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in direct recruitment to posts on the Railways is:
e: Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in direct recruitment on the Railways is 4 per cent of the vacancies.

q: The Permanent Negotiating Machinery (PNM) on the Railways is the forum for:

options.A: Negotiations between the Railway Administration and the recognised federations of railway employees on matters of common concern
options.B: Settlement of the compensation claims of railway passengers
options.C: Negotiation of contracts with the suppliers of stores
options.D: Fixation of freight rates in consultation with the Chambers of Commerce

e: The Permanent Negotiating Machinery is the recognised forum for negotiations between the Railway Administration and the recognised federations of railway employees on matters of common concern.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a canteen is required to be provided in a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed is more than:
e: Under the Factories Act, a canteen must be provided in a factory where the number of workers ordinarily employed is more than 250.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a crèche facility is required to be provided in a factory in which the number of women workers ordinarily employed is more than:
e: Under the Factories Act, a creche must be provided in a factory where the number of women workers ordinarily employed is more than 30.

q: Under Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the information which is exempt from disclosure is:

options.A: Personal information, the disclosure of which has no relationship to any public activity or interest, unless a larger public interest justifies its disclosure
options.B: Information relating to the allowances admissible to an officer
options.C: Information relating to the seniority list of the staff of an office
options.D: Information relating to the budget of a division

e: Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act exempts personal information whose disclosure has no relationship to any public activity or interest, unless a larger public interest justifies disclosure.

q: Special Casual Leave granted to a railway servant is treated as:

options.A: Debited to his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: A period of absence without leave salary
options.D: A period spent on duty, and it is not debited to any leave account

e: Special Casual Leave is treated as a period spent on duty; it is granted for specific purposes and is not debited to any leave account of the servant.

q: The total period of Hospital Leave that can be granted to a railway servant during his entire service shall not exceed:
e: Hospital Leave is subject to an overall limit of 28 months during the entire service of a railway servant.

q: A railway servant on tour remains absent from his headquarters for not more than 6 hours in a day. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day is:
e: Daily Allowance is graded by hours of absence from headquarters; for absence of not more than 6 hours in a day, it is admissible at 30 per cent of the full rate.

q: In a major penalty proceeding under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the charged railway servant is required to submit his written statement of defence within:

options.A: 5 days of the receipt of the memorandum of charges
options.B: 10 days of the receipt of the memorandum of charges
options.C: 15 days of the receipt of the memorandum of charges
options.D: 30 days of the receipt of the memorandum of charges

e: In a major penalty proceeding, the charged servant must submit his written statement of defence within 10 days of receiving the memorandum of charges.

q: The payment of subsistence allowance to a railway servant under suspension is subject to his furnishing a certificate that he:

options.A: Is residing at his headquarters during the period of suspension
options.B: Has not engaged a legal practitioner for his defence
options.C: Has surrendered his railway passes and Privilege Ticket Orders
options.D: Is not engaged in any other employment, business, profession or vocation during the period in question

e: Subsistence allowance during suspension is paid only on the servant furnishing a certificate that he is not engaged in any other employment, business, profession or vocation during that period.

q: Rule 13A of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 prohibits a railway servant from:

options.A: Giving or taking, or abetting the giving or taking of, dowry
options.B: Accepting any gift at the time of his own marriage
options.C: Attending a marriage ceremony while on duty
options.D: Marrying a person employed under a foreign Government

e: Rule 13A of the Conduct Rules prohibits a railway servant from giving or taking, or abetting the giving or taking of, dowry.

q: The prohibition of sexual harassment of women employees at the workplace is contained in the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 in:
e: The prohibition of sexual harassment of women employees at the workplace is contained in Rule 3C of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966.

q: Without the previous sanction of the competent authority, a railway servant shall not:

options.A: Contribute an article of a purely literary, artistic or scientific character to a newspaper
options.B: Own wholly or in part, or conduct or participate in the editing or management of, any newspaper or other periodical publication
options.C: Subscribe to a daily newspaper at his own cost
options.D: Listen to a broadcast of news relating to Government policies

e: Without previous sanction of the competent authority, a servant cannot own wholly or in part, or conduct or participate in the editing or management of, any newspaper or periodical publication.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 relating to criticism of Government, a railway servant shall not, in any radio broadcast, telecast or published document, make any statement of fact or opinion which has the effect of:

options.A: Praising a policy of the Government
options.B: Explaining factually a scheme of the Government
options.C: Reporting the proceedings of an official meeting
options.D: Adverse criticism of any current or recent policy or action of the Central Government or a State Government

e: The Conduct Rules bar a servant from making, in any broadcast, telecast or published document, any statement amounting to adverse criticism of a current or recent policy or action of the Central or a State Government.

q: A Pension Payment Order (PPO) is issued in two halves, which are:

options.A: The pensioner's half and the disburser's half
options.B: The Accounts half and the Audit half
options.C: The original half and the duplicate half
options.D: The pension half and the commutation half

e: A Pension Payment Order is issued in two halves: the pensioner's half retained by the pensioner and the disburser's half used by the disbursing authority for making payment.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 15 years of qualifying service. The death gratuity payable to his family is:
e: Death gratuity is graded by length of service; for qualifying service of 5 years or more but less than 20 years, as here with 15 years, it is 20 times the emoluments.

q: Where a railway pensioner dies after his retirement, family pension at the enhanced rate is payable to his family for a period of:

options.A: 10 years from the date of death of the pensioner, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 67 years, whichever is earlier
options.B: 7 years from the date of death of the pensioner, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 67 years, whichever is earlier
options.C: 5 years from the date of death of the pensioner, or till the deceased would have attained the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
options.D: 10 years in all cases, irrespective of the age of the deceased

e: After the death of a pensioner, family pension at the enhanced rate runs for 7 years from the date of death, or till the deceased would have attained 67 years of age, whichever is earlier.

q: The pension admissible to a railway servant on his retirement is calculated at 50 per cent of:

options.D: His emoluments or his average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial to him

e: Pension is calculated at 50 per cent of the emoluments or of the average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial to the retiring servant.

q: The additional quantum of pension admissible to a railway pensioner on attaining the age of 85 years is:
e: The additional quantum of pension increases with age; on attaining 85 years, the pensioner gets an additional pension of 30 per cent of the basic pension.

q: The maximum amount of family pension admissible at the normal rate under the 7th CPC dispensation is:
e: The maximum family pension at the normal rate is 30 per cent of the maximum pay under the 7th CPC, i.e., 30 per cent of Rs 2,50,000 = Rs 75,000 per month.

q: For the grant of a financial upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) scheme, the prescribed benchmark of grading in the Annual Performance Appraisal Report is:
e: For financial upgradation under the MACP scheme, the prescribed APAR benchmark is Very Good; upgradation is granted only to servants meeting that grading standard.

q: An annual increment in a pay level is admissible to a railway servant on 1st January or 1st July only if, as on that date, he has completed in that level a minimum service of:
e: Under the 7th CPC increment rules, an increment on 1 January or 1 July is admissible only if the servant has completed at least six months of service in that level as on that date.

q: A railway servant appointed as a fresh recruit is entitled to avail Leave Travel Concession every year during the first:
e: A fresh recruit is entitled to avail LTC every year during the first eight years of service; thereafter the normal block pattern of LTC applies.

q: A claim for arrears of pay and allowances of a railway servant, which has not been preferred within the period specified below from the date it became due, is treated as a time-barred claim:
e: A claim for arrears of pay and allowances not preferred within three years from the date it became due is treated as a time-barred claim under the rules.

q: For the purpose of reservation for Other Backward Classes, a person falls in the 'creamy layer' where the annual income of his parents from sources other than salary and agricultural land exceeds:
e: For OBC reservation, a person falls in the creamy layer where the annual income of his parents from sources other than salary and agricultural land exceeds Rs 8 lakh.

q: In direct recruitment to Level-1 (erstwhile Group 'D') posts on the Railways, the percentage of vacancies reserved for Course Completed Act Apprentices is:
e: In direct recruitment to Level-1 posts, 20 per cent of the vacancies are reserved for Course Completed Act Apprentices who have completed their apprenticeship training on the Railways.

q: Casual labour engaged on the open line (other than project casual labour) is granted temporary status on completion of continuous service of:
e: Casual labour engaged on the open line is granted temporary status on completion of 120 days of continuous service.

q: House Building Advance granted to a railway servant carries simple interest at the rate of:
e: House Building Advance now carries a single uniform simple interest rate of 7.44% per annum. (Source: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs OM No. I-17015/2(2)/2024/H.III dated 12.06.2024 (FY 2024-25), retained for FY 2025-26 vide MoHUA OM dated 27.03.2025.)

q: For computing the rate of Night Duty Allowance, the amount of basic pay and Dearness Allowance of the railway servant is divided by:
e: The hourly rate of Night Duty Allowance is computed by dividing the amount of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance by 200, before applying the prescribed weightage for night hours.

q: The Productivity Linked Bonus admissible to eligible railway employees for a year is computed as the equivalent of wages for:
e: The Productivity Linked Bonus admissible to eligible railway employees is computed as the equivalent of wages for 78 days, subject to the prescribed wage ceiling.

q: Where an application under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is received by a public authority but the information sought concerns another public authority, the application is required to be transferred to that other public authority within:
e: Under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act, an application concerning another public authority must be transferred to that authority within five days of its receipt.

q: The fee prescribed under the Right to Information Act, 2005 for obtaining a copy of a document of A-4 size is:
e: The RTI (Fee and Cost) Rules prescribe a fee of Rs 2 per page for obtaining a copy of a document of A-4 or A-3 size.

q: The maximum amount of monthly subscription that a subscriber may pay into the General Provident Fund shall not exceed:

options.C: Rs 5 lakh in a financial year

e: GPF subscription has a minimum of 6 per cent of emoluments, but the maximum a subscriber may pay is his total emoluments.

q: In regard to subscription to the Provident Fund by a railway servant during the period of his suspension, the correct position is that the subscription is:

options.A: Compulsory at the rate at which he was subscribing before suspension
options.B: Optional, and he may subscribe at a rate of his choice within the prescribed limits
options.C: Prohibited during the entire period of suspension
options.D: Recovered compulsorily from his subsistence allowance

e: During suspension, subscription to the Provident Fund is not compulsory; the suspended servant may subscribe at any rate of his choice within the prescribed limits.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The declaration of home town made by a railway servant for the purpose of Leave Travel Concession is treated as final.
2. A change in the declared home town can be permitted only in exceptional circumstances, with the approval of the Head of Department.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the home town declaration for LTC is treated as final, and a change can be permitted only in exceptional circumstances with the approval of the Head of Department.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding recovery of excess payment made to a railway servant:
1. Recovery of excess payment is impermissible against a railway servant who is due to retire within one year of the date of the order of recovery.
2. Recovery of excess payment is impermissible in every case, even where the excess payment was obtained by the railway servant by fraud or misrepresentation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct because recovery of excess payment is impermissible against an employee due to retire within one year; statement 2 is wrong because recovery remains permissible where the excess was obtained by fraud or misrepresentation.

q: Study leave is not ordinarily granted to a railway servant who is due to retire from service within:

options.A: 1 year of the date of his expected return to duty after the expiry of the leave
options.B: 3 years of the date of his expected return to duty after the expiry of the leave
options.C: 5 years of the date of his expected return to duty after the expiry of the leave
options.D: 6 months of the date of his expected return to duty after the expiry of the leave

e: Study leave is not ordinarily granted to a railway servant who is due to retire within three years of the date of his expected return to duty after the expiry of the leave.

q: A railway servant who is promoted from a lower post to a higher post is ordinarily placed on probation for a period of:
e: A railway servant promoted from a lower post to a higher post is ordinarily placed on probation for a period of one year.

q: Maternity leave admissible to a female railway servant who gets a child through surrogacy, as a commissioning mother, is:

options.B: Admissible for a maximum of 45 days only
options.C: Admissible only if the child is her first surviving child
options.D: Admissible for 180 days, as in the case of a normal delivery

e: A commissioning mother who gets a child through surrogacy is admissible maternity leave of 180 days, at par with the leave admissible in the case of a normal delivery.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 28 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 96,000 per month. The retirement gratuity admissible to him is:
e: Retirement gratuity = 1/4 of emoluments x completed six-monthly periods = Rs 24,000 x 56 (28 years) = Rs 13,44,000.

q: The amount of insurance cover admissible to the family of a Group 'A' railway servant who dies while in service, under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, is:
e: Under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the insurance cover admissible on death in service for a Group A employee is Rs 1,20,000.

q: On retirement from service, a railway servant may be permitted to retain the railway quarter allotted to him for a period of:
e: On retirement, a railway servant may be permitted to retain the railway quarter allotted to him for a period of four months on the prescribed terms.

q: A railway servant transferred in public interest from one station to another is entitled to draw an advance of pay equal to:
e: A railway servant transferred in public interest is entitled to an advance of pay equal to one month's pay, recoverable in instalments.

q: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, running staff are entitled, in a month, to four periods of rest of not less than the period specified below each, or five periods of not less than 22 consecutive hours each:
e: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, running staff are entitled in a month to four periods of rest of not less than 30 consecutive hours each, or five periods of not less than 22 consecutive hours each.

q: In a disciplinary case having a vigilance angle against a Group 'A' railway officer, the advice of the Central Vigilance Commission is obtained:

options.A: Only at the stage of issue of the charge memorandum
options.B: At two stages - before the issue of the charge memorandum and before the imposition of the penalty
options.C: Only after the penalty has been imposed
options.D: Only when the charged officer makes a request for it

e: In a disciplinary case with a vigilance angle against a Group A officer, the advice of the Central Vigilance Commission is obtained at two stages - before issue of the charge memorandum and before imposition of the penalty.

q: The period spent by a railway servant in undergoing a prescribed course of training is treated, for the purposes of his service, as a period spent on:
e: The period spent by a railway servant in undergoing a prescribed course of training is treated as a period spent on duty for service purposes.

q: The leave salary admissible to a railway servant during a period of study leave is equal to:

options.A: Nil, as study leave is without leave salary
options.B: Half of the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.C: 75% of the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.D: The leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay

e: The leave salary during study leave is equal to the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay, so full leave salary is payable during study leave.

q: For ensuring that family pension commences without delay after the death of a pensioner, the pension disbursing bank may credit the pension of a railway pensioner to:

options.A: An account opened in the name of any member of his family
options.B: A joint account operated by the pensioner with his or her spouse, to which family pension can be credited on the pensioner's death
options.C: An account opened in the name of his nominee for gratuity
options.D: An account opened in the name of the Head of Office last served by him

e: To ensure family pension starts without delay, the pension may be credited to a joint account operated by the pensioner with his or her spouse, to which family pension can be credited on the pensioner's death.

q: A widow who has been appointed to a railway post on compassionate grounds remarries. The correct position is that:

options.A: Her appointment is liable to be terminated on her remarriage
options.B: She is required to refund the salary drawn by her after the death of her husband
options.C: She continues in service; only the family pension, if any admissible to her, ceases on her remarriage
options.D: She is reverted to a lower post on her remarriage

e: Remarriage does not affect a compassionate appointment; the widow continues in service, and only the family pension, if any admissible to her, ceases on her remarriage.

q: A request by a railway servant for alteration of his date of birth as recorded in his service records can be entertained only if it is made within the period specified below of his entering service, and the error is shown to be a bona fide clerical error:
e: A request for alteration of date of birth can be entertained only if made within five years of entering service and the error is shown to be a bona fide clerical error.

q:
Consider the following statements about Extraordinary Leave (EOL) granted to a railway servant:
1. No leave salary is admissible to the railway servant during the period of Extraordinary Leave.
2. Extraordinary Leave can be granted only when no other kind of leave is admissible to the railway servant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 only is correct: no leave salary is admissible during Extraordinary Leave. Statement 2 is wrong because EOL can also be granted when other leave is due, including in combination with it, on the servant's request.

q: A temporary (refundable) advance sanctioned to a railway servant from the amount at his credit in the Provident Fund is ordinarily limited to:

options.A: One month's pay or the entire balance at his credit, whichever is less
options.B: Three months' pay or half the amount at his credit, whichever is less
options.C: Six months' pay or three-fourths of the amount at his credit, whichever is less
options.D: Twelve months' pay or the entire balance at his credit, whichever is less

e: A temporary (refundable) advance from the Provident Fund is ordinarily limited to three months' pay or half the amount at the subscriber's credit, whichever is less.

q: A subscriber who exits from the National Pension System on attaining the age of 60 years, and whose total accumulated pension wealth does not exceed Rs 5 lakh, is permitted to:

options.A: Withdraw the entire accumulated pension wealth as a lump sum, without purchasing any annuity
options.B: Withdraw only 20 per cent of the corpus as a lump sum
options.C: Withdraw only 40 per cent of the corpus as a lump sum
options.D: Withdraw nothing until the corpus exceeds Rs 5 lakh

e:
On exit from NPS at the age of 60, where the total accumulated pension wealth does not exceed Rs 5 lakh, the subscriber may withdraw the entire amount as a lump sum without purchasing any annuity.
Update: the full-withdrawal limit on normal exit at age 60 has since been raised to Rs 8 lakh; a corpus up to Rs 5 lakh, as in this question, remains fully withdrawable as lump sum. (Source: PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under NPS) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, notified 16.12.2025; PIB Release ID 2206763 dated 19.12.2025.)

q: The National Pension System is regulated in India by the:

options.B: Securities and Exchange Board of India
options.C: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
options.D: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India

e: The National Pension System is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

q: Which of the following is required of a railway servant under Rule 22 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to intoxicating drinks and drugs?

options.A: He may consume intoxicating drinks in a public place while off duty
options.B: He shall not appear in a public place in a state of intoxication
options.C: He may remain under the influence of an intoxicating drink during duty, provided his performance is not affected
options.D: The Rules impose no restriction on the use of intoxicating drugs

e: Rule 22 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 prohibits a railway servant from appearing in a public place in a state of intoxication, among other restrictions on intoxicating drinks and drugs.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant shall not use his position or influence, directly or indirectly, to secure employment for any member of his family in any company or firm.
2. A railway servant shall not permit his son, daughter or other dependent to accept employment with a private firm with which he has official dealings, without the previous sanction of the prescribed authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct under the Conduct Rules: a servant shall not use his position or influence to secure employment for a family member, nor permit a dependent to accept employment with a firm he deals with officially without previous sanction.

q: 'Withholding of promotion for a specified period' imposed on a railway servant under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is classified as a:

options.C: Penalty imposable only by the President
options.D: Penalty not included in the Rules

e: Withholding of promotion for a specified period is classified as a minor penalty under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.

q: Which of the following is NOT a penalty specified in the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules?

options.B: Recovery from pay of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused to the Railways

e: Warning is not one of the penalties specified in the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules; censure, recovery from pay and withholding of increments are specified penalties.

q: In a major penalty proceeding under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the charged railway servant is entitled to:

options.B: Inspect, and take extracts from, the official records and documents relied upon against him, as mentioned in the charge memorandum
options.C: Demand that the inquiry be held by a judicial magistrate
options.D: Engage a legal practitioner in every case as a matter of right

e: In a major penalty proceeding, the charged railway servant is entitled to inspect, and take extracts from, the official records and documents relied upon against him as mentioned in the charge memorandum.

q: The maximum amount of family pension admissible at the enhanced rate under the 7th CPC dispensation is:
e: Family pension at the enhanced rate is 50 per cent of the pay last drawn; with the maximum pay under the 7th CPC being Rs 2,50,000, the maximum enhanced family pension is Rs 1,25,000 per month.

q: A railway servant resigns from service after completing 12 years of qualifying service. In regard to his pensionary benefits, the correct position is that:

options.A: Gratuity is admissible to him, but pension is not admissible
options.B: Both pension and gratuity are admissible to him
options.C: Neither pension nor gratuity is admissible to him
options.D: Only family pension is admissible to his family

e: Resignation entails forfeiture of past service, so pension is not admissible; but gratuity is admissible where the servant has rendered qualifying service of five years or more, as here with 12 years.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the wage period fixed in respect of an employed person shall not exceed:
e: Under Section 4 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the wage period fixed in respect of an employed person shall not exceed one month.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker works in a factory for more than nine hours in any day or for more than forty-eight hours in any week, he is entitled, in respect of the overtime work, to wages at the rate of:

options.A: One and a half times his ordinary rate of wages
options.B: Twice his ordinary rate of wages
options.C: His ordinary rate of wages only
options.D: Three times his ordinary rate of wages

e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a worker who works for more than nine hours in a day or more than forty-eight hours in a week is entitled to wages at twice his ordinary rate for the overtime work.

q: For gazetted Group 'B' posts on the Railways filled by promotion from Group 'C', the proportion of vacancies normally filled through the Limited Departmental Competitive Examination (LDCE) is:
e: For gazetted Group B posts filled by promotion from Group C, 30 per cent of the vacancies are normally filled through the Limited Departmental Competitive Examination (LDCE).

q: Maternity leave granted to a female railway servant may be combined with:

options.A: Any other kind of leave due and admissible to her
options.B: No other kind of leave whatsoever

e: Maternity leave may be combined with any other kind of leave due and admissible to the female railway servant.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Work Related Illness and Injury Leave (WRIIL) is not debited to the leave account of a railway servant.
2. WRIIL is admissible only where the illness or injury necessitating hospitalisation is directly attributable to the official duties of the railway servant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Work Related Illness and Injury Leave is not debited to the leave account, and it is admissible only where the illness or injury necessitating hospitalisation is directly attributable to official duties.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 12 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 60,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family is:
e: For 11 years or more but less than 20 years of qualifying service, death gratuity is 20 times the emoluments: 20 x Rs 60,000 = Rs 12,00,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 22 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 88,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him is:
e: Retirement gratuity = 1/4 of emoluments x completed six-monthly periods = Rs 22,000 x 44 (22 years) = Rs 9,68,000.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after completing full qualifying service. His average emoluments are Rs 64,000 per month. His monthly pension will be:
e: Pension on retirement after full qualifying service = 50 per cent of average emoluments = 50 per cent of Rs 64,000 = Rs 32,000 per month.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 1,10,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate will be:
e: Family pension at the enhanced rate = 50 per cent of last basic pay = 50 per cent of Rs 1,10,000 = Rs 55,000 per month.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 40,000. He commutes 40 per cent of his pension. Taking the commutation value for his age on the next birthday as 8.446 for each rupee of annual pension commuted, the lump sum commuted value payable to him is:
e: Pension commuted per month = 40 per cent of Rs 40,000 = Rs 16,000; annual amount = Rs 1,92,000; lump sum = 1,92,000 x 8.446 = Rs 16,21,632.
